name: Herrenvolk democracy
summary: A political order that is democratic for one dominant racial or ethnic group and authoritarian toward others. Members of the dominant group vote, hold office and are treated as equals, while subordinate groups are excluded from citizenship and the franchise and held in an inferior legal status. The term comes from Pierre van den Berghe (1967) and is applied to the antebellum and Jim Crow US South, apartheid South Africa and Liberia.
scope: The racially circumscribed democracy described by van den Berghe, Vickery and Roediger, centred on the Confederate South (Stephens's Cornerstone Speech) and apartheid-era South Africa. It is a political form rather than a full programme, so economic, religious and foreign-policy questions are mostly unaddressed; those answers are inferences and the profile excludes Rhodesia's property-based franchise and the contested Israel case, and the Nazi use of 'Herrenvolk'.

keyFigures.name: Pierre van den Berghe
keyFigures.role: Sociologist who introduced the term in Race and Racism (1967).

keyFigures.name: Alexander H. Stephens
keyFigures.role: Confederate vice president whose Cornerstone Speech set out the racial premise of a white-only republic.

sources.title: Herrenvolk democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, origin of the term, cases, citizenship and franchise features, related concepts.

sources.title: Cornerstone Speech (Alexander Stephens, 1861), as described and quoted in the article
sources.author: Wikipedia, quoting Alexander H. Stephens
sources.usedFor: Stated racial-hierarchy premise of the Confederacy, rejection of racial equality, slavery as cause of secession.

sources.title: 'Herrenvolk' Democracy and Egalitarianism in South Africa and the U.S. South (opening extract)
sources.author: Kenneth P. Vickery, Comparative Studies in Society and History 16(3), 1974
sources.usedFor: Only the opening paragraph was readable: egalitarian ideals coexisting with racial exclusion by treating some groups as outside the people.

sources.title: Apartheid
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Racial classification, segregation statutes, franchise limits, forced removals, mixed-marriage bans, security laws.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; white-only welfare provision fits the model but whether it is state-run varied between the antebellum South and apartheid-era states.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: white-labour protection (job reservation) mattered more than wage floors across races, and Jim Crow Southern elites resisted wage regulation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Regimes mixed racial labour controls with market economies; the sources describe no single economic doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; settler regimes combined private property with state intervention for the dominant group, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated position; egalitarianism applies only within the dominant group, and the sources say nothing on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: unions were typically white-only or colour-barred, and the Colour Bar Act kept Black workers from skilled trades, so labour organising served the dominant group only.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: land acts reserved ownership by race, which treats property rights as strong for the dominant group; the sources do not state a general doctrine.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no consistent view across the regimes cited.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not documented; the model gives the dominant group benefits while excluding others, but does not fix a view on welfare level.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Southern planter and settler-state economies rested on racially bound labour, not worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era security laws (Terrorism Act, Internal Security Act) gave wide powers against the subordinate group.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; no link between the model and drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: a regime resting on open racial-hierarchy claims, as in Stephens's speech, would not restrict them; it would restrict speech against the order.

strong-leader.rationale: Not addressed; Herrenvolk regimes kept elections and legislatures for the dominant group, but strong executives occurred too.

state-harmful.rationale: Inferred: the model depends on a state enforcing racial classification, segregation and disenfranchisement, so abolishing it contradicts the system.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: armed dominant-group citizens served as a safeguard of the racial order in the Jim Crow South; restriction was applied to the subordinate group.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: enforcement of pass laws, group areas and segregation relied on police and military authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: weakly; apartheid's Immorality Acts policed sexual conduct, though the sources discuss only the interracial side.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: states' rights was a Confederate theme (Stephens), yet apartheid centralised racial law nationally.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: harsh coercive treatment of the subordinate group is typical, but the sources do not discuss penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: the marriage bans and racial-purity concerns imply a conservative family order; no source states it directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the conservative social orders involved; the ideology itself is silent on it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents' views varied by era and region.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred: Stephens invoked scripture for racial hierarchy and apartheid drew on Christian national ideas, though the model does not require it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The system is founded on racial hierarchy, so remedying racial subordination is the opposite of its aim; Stephens held racial inequality to be natural.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the ideology treats racial categories as natural and fixed, and the same naturalising habit would extend to gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The dominant group's culture and status are what the regime protects; membership in the 'people' is defined by the dominant group.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: dominant-group defenders resisted rapid reform, citing established racial law.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: restricted citizenship and descent-based nationality laws (Liberia, the 1790 US naturalization law) limit membership to the dominant group; selective rather than general.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: outside bodies challenged these regimes; apartheid South Africa and the Confederacy defended their sovereignty.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; no consistent trade doctrine. Stephens's Confederate constitution barred tariffs, but apartheid South Africa was protectionist.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred: the model puts the dominant group's interests first, but the sources do not discuss foreign policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: foreign human-rights intervention was a threat to these regimes, so adherents oppose it.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from descent-based citizenship and racial restriction on membership.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; settler-state economies pursued growth. Inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no position follows from the model.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to the model.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: secession was justified by the Confederacy, but violent overthrow of the racial order is treated as a threat; adherents would reject revolution by the subordinate group.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred: the 'democratic' side of the model gives the dominant group a vote and an egalitarian self-image, so expert rule over the public is disfavoured.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: the regimes were capitalist or planter economies with private property; no source discusses planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: no public-ownership tradition among adherents.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not discussed in any source on the model; land policy here concerns who may own land by race, not how it is taxed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The sources say nothing about estate taxation; the model concerns who holds political rights, not inheritance policy.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a benefit restricted to the dominant group fits the model, but nothing is stated.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Split: Confederate texts oppose tariffs, apartheid-era policy was protectionist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed by sources; apartheid South Africa had heavy state direction, the antebellum South little.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: the egalitarian side of Herrenvolk republicanism favoured broad white property-holding, though planters held concentrated wealth.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: the model is compatible with capitalism and incompatible with abolishing wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside what the sources describe, so adherents have no common view.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; colour-bar bargaining existed in South Africa but is not a defining position.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mixed: the Solid South and apartheid South Africa were effectively one-party within the dominant group, but the model is defined by elections among that group.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: republican and settler-democratic traditions dominate the cited cases; Stephens built a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents hold that government by and for the dominant group's voters is legitimate; democracy is real for the master group but not extended to others.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums versus representation is not covered; the model only requires that the dominant group vote.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: incompatible with the dominant group's parliamentary and elected-office system.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Confederacy's founding was an act of secession; Stephens defended it as protecting the racial order.

natural-rulers.rationale: Stephens states that subordination to the 'superior race' is the natural and normal condition of Black people, which asserts that some are naturally fit to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Inferred: enforcing racial order and disenfranchisement relied on violence and repression.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source ties the model to a view of war's moral effects.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents varied between a church-backed order and secular settler states.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Stephens invoked scripture for hierarchy, but laws were passed by legislatures of the dominant group, so not a general scripture-law position.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: the racial order was enforced by the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred: settler regimes defending minority or racial rule valued military strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The model gives full political membership only to one ethnic group and treats the subordinate group as outside the political nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Inferred: Herrenvolk republicanism puts racial solidarity above class lines among the dominant group.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: equality is applied inside the dominant group and denied between groups.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: land acts limited Black ownership and reserved most land for the dominant group.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: the ideology rejects redress for racial subordination.

civilizational-union.rationale: The model concerns one state's internal racial order, not union with other states by civilization.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; the model protects rights for the dominant group.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is unrelated to the model and no source addresses it.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: Not a doctrine; dominant groups feared losing demographic share, favouring numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: modernising settler economies do not support rejecting industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological pace is not part of the model; no source states a view.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic to the historical cases and unrelated to the racial-franchise model.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the historical cases predate algorithmic governance.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; the cases predate modern encryption and sources do not discuss it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mixed: defenders of Jim Crow and apartheid preserved existing order, not necessarily a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: the system rests on a stated racial principle, not on pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred: dominant-group politics ran through elections and legislatures.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not discuss whether methods should mirror aims; the regimes used coercion alongside elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: incompatible with settler agricultural and industrial economies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: the colour bar enforced a racial division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: distribution followed racial status, as with job reservation and land acts.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend the prevailing property system and its racially bound labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred: communism was suppressed in apartheid South Africa.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: private white farm ownership was protected; land acts barred others.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: adherents defended the existing economic order.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on tax vary.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred: the apartheid statutes policed sexual relations and association across race with no harm rationale.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are assigned by group membership in the model, not held by individuals as such.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; some regimes conscripted white men.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: the model prizes the vote for the dominant group.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: the model rests on political membership and citizenship, not customer status.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred: liberty as non-interference for the dominant group, restricted for others.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and university influence is not discussed in the sources on the model.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Stephens grounds racial hierarchy in nature ('great physical, philosophical, and moral truth') and the model rests on racial hierarchy being innate.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: representation by party and elected office for dominant-group voters.

total-state.rationale: Inferred: the model includes elections and civic freedoms for the dominant group.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth narratives belong to other nationalisms; the sources do not present this as part of the model.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the Confederacy and settler states did expand, but it is not defining.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: authority rests on elections among the dominant group.

bound-labor.rationale: Stephens defends slavery and the colour bar tied Black labour; the statement as worded is feudal, so the fit is partial.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: Stephens claims racial hierarchy as objective truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Mixed: adherents appeal to natural law yet reject the Declaration's universal equality.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; common good applies to the dominant group.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Scholars debate whether Israel counts as Herrenvolk; the ideology itself takes no position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Liberia's descent-based citizenship hints at it, but the sources take no position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed in the sources on the model.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: democracy is for political membership, not companies.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not addressed; sources discuss only racial segregation of schooling at most.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed in the sources, and the cases span very different eras and economies.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not tie the model to a doctrine linking political and economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: law and elections are the model's instruments.

national-self-determination.rationale: Stephens and apartheid-era leaders asserted the dominant group's right to self-rule; the statement concerns nations, and subordinates are not treated as nations with equal claims.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: apartheid South Africa resisted international oversight.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Stephens appealed to both science and scripture, so adherents are not committed to reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Citizenship was tied to the dominant group, so benefits reserved for citizens effectively reserved them for that group.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditions are not discussed; the sources are about who is included, not what conditions apply.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred: racial solidarity across classes within the dominant group is the model's egalitarian side.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: the regimes stood with or within the Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: white workers aligned by race and nation rather than internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred: conservative gender order in the Confederacy and Jim Crow South; franchise in the model was often male.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The apartheid state classified people by race and legislated separate residence (Group Areas Act) and public amenities (Reservation of Separate Amenities Act).

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: the state is held to serve the dominant group, which cuts across class, rather than the ruling class alone.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for most cases and not addressed by sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Split: assimilation applied to those of the dominant group, while the subordinate group was kept apart.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: fear of demographic loss is a theme of dominant-group politics, but not documented in these sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: majoritarian systems used within the dominant group; the Solid South was winner-take-all.

national-mission.rationale: Stephens claims a world-historical first, but not a mission to spread it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend conventional gender order.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mixed: populist rhetoric appears in Herrenvolk republicanism, but adherents hold office.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; racial concerns present but not disability policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era leaders defended security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: the states enforced racial law extensively.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Prohibition of Mixed Marriages Act of 1949 and the Immorality Amendment Act of 1950 criminalised marriage and sex across race lines in apartheid South Africa.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Stephens rejects the Declaration's equality premise, calling the idea of equal races 'an error' and the unequal status of Black people the cornerstone of the Confederacy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: adherents see their states as legitimate; scholars apply the label, adherents reject it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: separate legal regimes by group.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion law is not part of the model as the sources describe it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Unrelated to the model and not discussed in the sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schooling is not addressed by the sources used.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; socialism is not the model's frame.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Split: consent applies only to the dominant group, while the governed majority is excluded.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance doctrine is not discussed, and the cases had different trade policies.

population-transfer.rationale: Apartheid forced removals (about 3.5 million between 1960 and 1983) moved Black Africans to bantustans.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred: state coercion in service of racial order is accepted.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources do not state a view on competition as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Suppression of Communism Act (1950) shows outlawing parties that threatened the order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The model accepts arbitrary rule over the subordinate group while claiming freedom for the dominant one.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; Confederate constitution was drawn on the US model.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: priority goes to the dominant group.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are not addressed and are anachronistic for the historical cases.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: the colour-bar order sought to control Black labour action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: No source ties the model to a theory of poverty's causes.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The model treats the subordinate group as outside the political nation and holds that the dominant group must remain demarcated.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: elections among the dominant group are the method.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: security laws (Terrorism Act, Internal Security Act) allowed suspension for the regime.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price control in scarcity is not discussed by the sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mixed: censorship existed in apartheid South Africa but the model includes free press for the dominant group.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred: restricted citizenship laws (Naturalization Act of 1790, Liberia).

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not discussed; officials of the dominant group were not tied to worker wages.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not discussed; the model concerns who may vote, not how parties bind members.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of forces is not stated as part of the model; the cases varied between presidents and parliaments.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to the model in the sources.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: authority rests on elected dominant-group officials.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: loyalty to the dominant-group state.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Art censorship is not discussed in the sources on the model.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Stephens proposed a single six-year presidential term, but this is not core.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not addressed in the sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed in the sources, and the cases differed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed dominant-group citizens appeared in Southern militia traditions, but not a stated doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian ideals appear in the Southern case only.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The model concerns internal racial order, not reunifying divided nations.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual attitudes are not part of the model as documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Stephens asserts a natural hierarchy of races and apartheid ranked groups, which contradicts treating cultures as merely different.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: harsh punishment for the subordinate group was typical.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; some religious fit but no source states it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: apartheid South Africa censored publications; weakly supported.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Liberia limited birthright citizenship by descent from Americo-Liberians and the US limited citizenship to 'free white persons'; citizenship follows group descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: weakly; apartheid-era Bantu Education imposed separate schooling.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions from law are not addressed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: conformity to the racial order.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend the economic system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; assemblies were used (Confederate convention) but only for the dominant group.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Development-driven restrictions on freedom are not discussed; restrictions here serve racial order.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; South Africa did develop weapons but not as a doctrine of the model.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mode of choosing the head of state is not specified in the sources; the cases used various methods.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in the sources on the model.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not discussed in the sources used.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: property rights are held strongly.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist classification dispute with no bearing on the model, and no source addresses it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic for the historical cases and not addressed by sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not discussed in the sources on the model.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: Herrenvolk regimes ruled populations without their consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state hierarchy is not addressed by sources on the model.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of the head of state above party is not specified by the model.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: Confederate adherents defended secession against the Union.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; bantustans gave limited autonomy but under control.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is not discussed by the sources on the model.

character-from-environment.rationale: Stephens rests racial hierarchy on 'great physical' truth and the model treats racial status as innate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: constitutional government for the dominant group.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic for the historical cases and not addressed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The sources do not describe any mixed-constitution doctrine, only a republican form for the dominant group.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: republican egalitarianism within the dominant group.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in the sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: land acts concentrated land with the dominant group; redistribution to the subordinate group was resisted.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The model concerns rule within a state's borders, not claims on territory abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not part of the model as the sources describe it; Christian-settler regimes did not typically punish apostasy.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed in the sources on the model.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The sources do not link the model to cross-border unions of kindred peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: weakly; separate institutions were imposed, not offered as autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: the subordinate group is denied equal rights in the model.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: race is treated as the driving fact.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources on the model.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The model gives the dominant-group majority the final say, and Dred Scott shows courts upholding the racial order; the statement fits partly.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not part of the model, and the cases traded with the world.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreement standards are anachronistic for most cases and not discussed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Group-based racial privilege is hereditary, but titles are not discussed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Stephens presents subordination to the 'superior race' as natural and beneficial, and apartheid rule was justified as guardianship.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: identity education for the dominant group.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: adherents oppose preferences that help the subordinate group, but favour group preferences for themselves; partial.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money-creation policy is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not address capitalist crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy influence is not part of the model as the sources describe it.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: integration into the world economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources do not address world-systems exploitation of labour, though white labour privilege is a related scholarly theme.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Jim Crow-era private discrimination was enforced and defended; the statement asks about private liberty, which was partially claimed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; rights were entrenched but only for the dominant group.

elective-rulers.rationale: The model is defined by elected office among the dominant group; Confederate government was republican.

minority-veto.rationale: Calhoun-style veto is a Southern theme but is not discussed in these sources.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not addressed; the Confederacy justified secession differently, and the sources give no general doctrine.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: elected legislatures of the dominant group make law.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is unrelated to the model and not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is unrelated to the model and not discussed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist duty of the privileged appears in some Southern thought, but the sources do not state it for the model.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The model values political participation for the dominant group.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim with no bearing on the sources used.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The sources do not address hegemony theory as part of the model.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: adherents see their economies as legitimate.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: offices belonged to the dominant group; weakly stated.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question; unrelated to the model.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not part of the model as the sources describe it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparisons of fascism and communism are not addressed, and adherents' views vary.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Stephens states that slavery was the 'immediate cause' of secession and its racial premise the cornerstone of the Confederacy.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues policy is not addressed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The sources do not discuss whether political institutions suit every civilization, though settlers exported their own forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Political role of armed forces is not specified for the model.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care-work policy is not addressed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial obligation is not discussed in the sources on the model.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: offices by election within the dominant group.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign investment screening is not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed in the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mandated delegates are not part of the model as documented.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: private ownership by the dominant group.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: elected legislatures of the dominant group control spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources, and the cases included multilingual dominant groups, such as Afrikaans and English in South Africa.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; land laws were racial rather than foreign.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: adherents reject treating unequal racial outcomes as discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumption critique is not part of the model as described.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign support is not addressed in the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc discipline is not part of the model as described.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is not addressed in the sources on the model.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era restrictions on foreign support to opposition.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family incentives are not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Group Areas and land acts restricted ownership by race and locality.

job-guarantee.rationale: Job reservation for whites existed (colour bar), but a general guarantee is not discussed.

democratic-peace.rationale: International-relations theory is not addressed in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: adherents hold the legal order to be binding on the subordinate group.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era states opposed outside intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources, beyond colour-bar labour rules.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not documented in the sources used.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: marriage law was used to maintain racial lines.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not addressed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not part of the model as described.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: apartheid South Africa rejected external legal oversight.

religious-nation.rationale: Stephens cited scripture, but the community was defined by race, not religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Stephens favoured local funding of local projects but it is not a defining stand.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A Marxist formulation not addressed by sources; the model protects private property generally, not distinguishing means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Suppression of Communism Act (1950) shows hostility to communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery is not addressed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not part of the model as described.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed; the cases generally disregarded or overrode them, but the sources give no doctrine.

majority-settlement.rationale: The sources do not describe settlement policy as part of the model, apart from forced removals under apartheid.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical claims are not addressed in the sources; settler regimes rested on present control and law instead.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; the term itself is rooted in German racial rhetoric, but adherents are not defined by this.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sexual-orientation law is not addressed in the sources on the model.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Apartheid security laws suppressed opposition; the model gives dominant group elections but suppresses subordinate-group politics.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not discussed in the sources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The model concerns rule inside a state, not colonial economics.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine unrelated to the model.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A religious-legitimacy doctrine unrelated to the model.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; participation is real for the dominant group.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: oppression is denied or defended.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is not addressed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The sources do not take a view on the left-right spectrum.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend the existing labour system.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The sources do not discuss Islam, and the model concerns racial rather than religious boundaries.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stephens appeals to nature and scripture, but authority is constitutional.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not addressed in the sources.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not addressed and is anachronistic for the cases.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources do not describe an economic model; adherents' regimes ranged widely.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: enforcement of racial order requires armed force.

rich-first.rationale: Staged development is not discussed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc alignment is not discussed; apartheid South Africa aligned with the West at times, but the sources give no doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit-system reform is not addressed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Lender conditionality is not addressed in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: The franchise is defined by group membership, not property, in the central cases (though Rhodesia used economic qualifications).

racial-franchise.rationale: The defining feature of the model is a franchise and office-holding limited to the dominant group, as with the 1910 and 1936 South African franchise rules and the US 'free white persons' standard.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the order concerns race, and its dominant-group ideology (the Cornerstone Speech) rests on hierarchy, not on ending domination of women or nature.

reification.rationale: Inferred: the sources describe a racial hierarchy defended as natural, with no critique of market society as disguising social relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: the dominant group sees its own formal rights as real and equal, so adherents would not call them hollow, though the sources do not address press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: equals within the dominant group are ruled by common law and equal rights, while subordinate groups are not; the sources do not discuss decree versus standing law.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the sources concern racial limits on citizenship and do not address how participation is carried out.

open-government-data.rationale: The sources do not discuss open records; the order is defined by who may take part, not how records are kept.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The order restricts by race, and marriage bans (miscegenation laws) follow race; religion is not its defining line, so adherents are neither clearly for nor against.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Racial exclusion is central but the statement concerns a religious minority; the sources do not address it and adherents are not clearly split either way.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the order values voting and office-holding by the dominant group through ordinary elections, not assemblies chosen by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the Cornerstone Speech and defenders of the order appealed to settled authority and scripture, which suggests a preference for inherited doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Adherents are split: equality among members of the dominant group fits a rough equality of means, but planter and industrial elites kept their fortunes; the sources do not settle it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the regimes the term describes were socially conservative and did not allow open service by gay and lesbian people; not addressed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: apartheid and the antebellum South justified the racial order in religious terms, so state-promoted atheism is opposed; the sources do not discuss it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the model relies on policing and coercion of the subordinate group, as in apartheid's pass laws, so abolishing police and prisons is opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the model reserves power for the dominant group rather than sharing it among communities, so it rejects sharing, though it also rejects simple majority rule where the dominant group is a minority.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; white-only welfare and reliance on private help both occurred in the regimes described.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; term limits have no bearing on the model.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the model restricts the franchise to the dominant group and does not favour widening participation through delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; extinction risk is anachronistic to the regimes described.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the societies described were patriarchal and church leadership was male; religious office is not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: egalitarianism in this model covers men of the dominant group, and the societies described were patriarchal; marriage is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The model confines the franchise to the dominant group and denies it to others who live in the territory, so non-citizen residents would not vote.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the model is a political form with no stated housing policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the model protects property of the dominant group, including slaves in the antebellum South, so abolishing property rights in ideas is unlikely.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated position on youth organisation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the antebellum South and not addressed for apartheid South Africa.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no consistent position across the cases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the model denies the dominant group's wrongs against subordinate peoples, so formal recognition of such killings is unlikely.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the Confederate and apartheid orders relied on property in land and slaves, and the sources do not address income principles.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the order was enforced by force against the subordinate group, but the sources do not state a view on killing in self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on national origin varied between the US South and Afrikaner nationalism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's conventional view of sex as biological, which the sources do not discuss.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the order's reliance on fixed group categories for the dominant group's equality.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the Confederate and Afrikaner traditions honoured their dead as heroes, though the sources do not describe this directly.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not addressed; religious framing varied between cases, and the sources describe a political form.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the model concerns people living in a territory they control, not a homeland for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the model is built on state-enforced political and legal rules, not on cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional religion of the dominant group in both main cases.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the model's defence of existing religion, with the main cases using scripture to justify hierarchy.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Apartheid job reservation and the Jim Crow South kept skilled work and economic positions for the dominant group, which may be a numerical minority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from apartheid's consolidation of separate territories for each group, which the sources describe only in outline.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: apartheid-era unions were racially divided and job reservation protected white workers; independent unions are not a stated principle.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: the model protects the dominant group's privileges, not working-class power as such.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the model describes who votes, not how the legislature is built.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the Confederate order rested on private property, including property in slaves.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; the Confederacy stressed state sovereignty but apartheid South Africa was centralised.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: the order protected the dominant group's households, but the sources do not discuss wage levels.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: pass laws and surveillance of the subordinate group imply state tracing of its movement and money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the same control of the subordinate group; the sources do not mention online matters.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: the Cornerstone Speech says inequality is natural and the subordinate race is fitted for subordination, treating people as means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: Stephens appeals to divine ordering of the races, and apartheid was justified by church doctrine.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the Confederate case rested on states' rights that the central government could not remove.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The model is politics organised around the dominant racial group's interests, with full rights for it and exclusion for others.

racial-pride.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech holds that the dominant race is superior, which implies pride in it as a given.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; both the Confederacy and apartheid South Africa fought wars, and no principle on force is stated.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Membership in the dominant group is defined by race or descent rather than language and history, so the model rejects shared language as a basis of nationhood; inferred from the model's racial basis.

communal-electorates.rationale: The model excludes subordinate groups from the franchise rather than giving them separate religious electorates; apartheid's separate racial rolls were a form of exclusion, not religious communal voting.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Dominant-group regimes such as apartheid South Africa portrayed themselves as threatened by outside forces; inferred from the apartheid article, not a defining part of the model.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; provision for the dominant group could be public or private, so adherents are split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental policy is not addressed by the model or its sources.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; concern for the dominant group's heirs does not imply any environmental position.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The model rests on a hierarchy of groups and on the dominant group's shared equality, not on gendered values; inferred at low confidence.

arms-reduction.rationale: Regimes of this kind relied on armed force to maintain control over a subordinate majority or population, which implies resistance to reducing arms; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; diplomatic practice varied among the regimes the term describes.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the model is a political form compatible with varied economic policies.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; the dominant group's own militias and armed citizens were tolerated or encouraged while subordinate groups were disarmed, so the model is split on a general state monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the model treats citizen-soldiers of the dominant group as the guardians of the order, so a general duty to refuse state wars does not fit.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; dominant-group unions often bargained collectively but excluded subordinate groups, and the form does not settle the question.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: welfare for the dominant group was sometimes generous, but top-up credits for the low-paid are not part of the model.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the political form says nothing about borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the order defends the existing hierarchy of groups, and it was hostile to reordering rules in favour of poorer, mostly non-dominant peoples.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the dominant group runs the existing state for its own benefit, so adherents want to keep and use it, not destroy it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: the model requires a fixed legal and racial order, not open experimentation with economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no position follows from the political form.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the dominant group is treated as the enduring people to which the state belongs, though the sources do not describe it as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: a low-priority redistribution not tied to the model, and unlikely to be favoured by its adherents.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: adherents frame the system as legitimate rule by the dominant group, not as exploitation of a periphery.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech rejects racial equality and builds the state on a natural hierarchy of groups, so a shared human nature grounding equal dignity is denied.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: state media under the apartheid and Confederate-era orders served the dominant group, so independence from government was not a goal.

missingStatements.text: The right to vote and hold office should be limited to members of one racial or ethnic group.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining feature of the model is a franchise and office-holding limited to the dominant group, as with the 1910 and 1936 South African franchise rules and the US 'free white persons' standard.

missingStatements.text: A country can rightly be called a democracy even if part of its resident population is denied the vote.
missingStatements.rationale: Herrenvolk democracy holds that a regime is democratic for the master group while ruling the rest dictatorially; van den Berghe's formulation treats this as a democratic form.
missingStatements.declined: Definitional question of whether such a regime counts as a democracy; narrow, and racial-franchise tests the substance.

notes: Many adherents did not call themselves 'Herrenvolk democrats'; the term is analytic and was coined by scholars, so the profile reflects regimes' stated principles and statutes. Most economic, religious and foreign-policy answers are low-confidence inferences, and the salience check may exclude this profile.
